title: Leopold Mozart Takes His Children on Tour
text:
Leopold Mozart was a violinist and composer at the court of the Archbishop of Salzburg and the author of a respected violin method. When he realized how gifted his two children were, his daughter Maria Anna, called Nannerl, and his son Wolfgang, he devoted himself to their training and their careers.

In June 1763, when Wolfgang was seven and Nannerl twelve, the whole family set out on a tour that lasted three and a half years. They traveled by coach through Munich, Mannheim, Brussels and Paris, where they played at Versailles, and on to London, where they stayed more than a year and Wolfgang met Johann Christian Bach. The children played for kings and paying audiences. Wolfgang performed tricks such as playing on a keyboard covered with a cloth, and wrote his first symphonies.

Leopold's long letters home to his landlord in Salzburg, Lorenz Hagenauer, record the money, the illnesses and the triumphs. In The Hague, in 1765, first Nannerl and then Wolfgang fell dangerously ill, and Nannerl was given the last rites. Both recovered, and the family returned to Salzburg in November 1766.

Leopold gave up much of his own career for his son. The bond was close but heavy. When Wolfgang, as a grown man, settled in Vienna and married Constanze Weber against his father's wishes, their relationship cooled, though they kept writing until Leopold's death in 1787.
lesson: Investing everything in a gifted child can open the world to them. But a parent's ambition must eventually give way to the child's own life.
people: Leopold Mozart, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Nannerl Mozart
location: Salzburg, Austria; Paris, France; London, UK; The Hague, Netherlands
source: The Letters of Mozart and His Family, trans. Emily Anderson (1938)
